english.synthetic: Written for tests. No real patient, no real person.

segments.text: Good day, Mr. Popa. How are you feeling now compared to last time?
Good day. Not very well, Mr. doctor. The cough hasn't gone away and for three days I've had a fever, thirty-eight and something in the evening.
Are you coughing up phlegm?
Yes, mostly in the morning, it's green. And I get very tired, barely make it to the second floor.
Do you still smoke?
I've reduced to ten cigarettes a day, but I haven't quit altogether.
Let me listen to your lungs. Breathe deeply through your mouth. One more time.
It hurts a bit on the right side when I breathe deeply.
I hear some crackles at the base of the right lung. I want a chest X-ray today or at the latest tomorrow.
Where do I get it done?
At the county hospital, radiology. I'll give you the referral form now and you call to schedule an appointment.
Okay. And what about the fever?
I'll prescribe amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, one thousand milligrams, twice a day, for seven days. For the fever take paracetamol, no more than four tablets a day.
Can I go to work? I work on a construction site.
No. I'll give you a sick leave for five days, up to Tuesday inclusive. Rest and plenty of fluids.
I need a certificate for my employer.
I'll issue the medical leave certificate now, you take it to human resources.
Thank you. And the tests?
You'll also do a hematology panel and C-reactive protein test, tomorrow morning, on an empty stomach.
I'll do them tomorrow. When should I come back?

I'll be waiting for you on Tuesday, November 10th, at half past eight, with the X-ray and test results. If you have trouble breathing or the fever goes above thirty-nine, come immediately or call the emergency department.
I understand. And about smoking?
I recommend the smoking cessation program at the clinic. I'll put you on the list and the assistant, Mrs. Elena, will call you next week.
Okay, I'll try. Thank you, Mr. doctor.
